(p-225) Sūrat "Fuṣṣilat" (Sura 41)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Ḥā-Mīm﴾. If you make it the name of the sura, it is a subject (mubtada'), and ﴿A revelation﴾ is its predicate (khabar). If you make it an enumeration of the letters, then "A revelation" is the predicate of an omitted subject (mubtada' maḥdhūf), and "a Book" is either a substitute (badal) for "a revelation," or a predicate following a predicate, or the predicate of an omitted subject, or "a revelation" is the subject (mubtada'),

﴿from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ is its qualifier (ṣifah).

(p-225) Sūrat "Fuṣṣilat" (Sura 41)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Ḥā-Mīm﴾. If you make it the name of the sura, it is a subject (mubtada'), and ﴿A revelation﴾ is its predicate (khabar). If you make it an enumeration of the letters, then "A revelation" is the predicate of an omitted subject (mubtada' maḥdhūf), and "a Book" is either a substitute (badal) for "a revelation," or a predicate following a predicate, or the predicate of an omitted subject, or "a revelation" is the subject (mubtada'),

﴿from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ is its qualifier (ṣifah).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 3:

﴿Kitāb﴾ (a Book), its predicate is ﴿fuṣṣilat āyātuhu﴾ (its verses have been made distinct). That is: they have been differentiated and made into detailed explanations in various meanings, of rulings (aḥkām), parables (amthāl), admonitions (mawā'iz), promise (wa'd), threat (wa'īd), and other than that.

﴿Qur'ānan ʿarabiyyan﴾ (an Arabic Qur'an) is in the accusative (manṣūb) by way of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) and praise (madḥ). That is: by this detailed Book is meant a Qur'an whose attributes are such-and-such. Or it is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl), meaning: its verses have been made distinct while being an Arabic Qur'an.

﴿Li-qawmin yaʿlamūn﴾ (for a people who know). That is: for a people of Arabs, who know what was sent down to them of the detailed verses, clarified in their Arabic tongue. And "li-qawmin" is connected either to "tanzīl" or to "fuṣṣilat": that is, "a revelation from Allah for their sake," or "its verses have been made distinct for them." The most apparent view is that it is a qualifier like what comes before it and what comes after it, that is: "an Arabic Qur'an existing for an Arab people."

﴿Bashīran wa-nadhīran﴾ (as a bearer of good news and a warner) are two attributes (ṣifatān) of ﴿Qur'ānan﴾ (a Qur'an).

﴿Fa-a'rada aktharuhum fa-hum lā yasma'ūn﴾ means: they do not accept it (lā yaqbalūn). This is like your saying, "تَشَفَّعْتُ إلى فُلانٍ فَلَمْ يَسْمَعْ قَوْلِي" (*tashaffa'tu ilā fulān fa-lam yasma' qawlī*, "I interceded with so-and-so, but he did not listen to my words"). In fact he heard it, but since he did not accept it and did not act upon what it required, it is as though he had not heard it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 6:

﴿Say: "I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is one God."﴾ This is an answer to their saying: "Our hearts are in coverings" (akinnah). Its meaning is that he said to them: "I am not an angel. I am only a human being like you, but it has been revealed to me apart from you. So my prophethood is established by the revelation made to me, and I am a human being. When my prophethood is established, it becomes obligatory upon you to follow me, and what is revealed to me is that your God is one God."

﴿So take the straight path to Him﴾: be upright toward Him with monotheism (tawhid) and sincerity in worship, not turning right or left, and not inclining toward what Satan adorns for you of taking allies and intercessors.

﴿And seek His forgiveness﴾: for shirk.

﴿And woe to the polytheists﴾.

Surah 41, verse 7: Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil)

﴿Those who do not give the zakat﴾: they do not believe in the obligation of zakat, nor do they give it; or they do not do that by which they would become purified (zakiyya'), namely faith.

﴿And they are disbelievers in the Hereafter﴾: in the resurrection (ba'th), the reward (thawab), and the punishment (iqab).

﴿They are disbelievers.﴾ The withholding of zakat has been linked with disbelief in the Hereafter only because wealth is the dearest thing to a person, being the very companion of his soul (shaqiq ruhihi). So when he expends it in the way of Allah, that is the strongest proof of his uprightness, the sincerity of his intention, and the purity of his inner disposition. The "mu'allafa qulubuhum" (those whose hearts are to be won over) were deceived only by a morsel of this world; so their partisanship was soothed and their obstinacy was softened. And the Banu Hanifa apostatised only through withholding zakat. In this there is an incitement for the believers to pay zakat and a severe warning against withholding it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 8:

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—for them is a reward never to be cut off.﴾ "Ghayr mamnun" means uninterrupted, cut off. It was said: it was revealed concerning the sick, the chronically disabled, and the elderly who are unable to perform acts of obedience; for them the reward is recorded as if they were doing it in their best state of health.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 9:

﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days﴾, (the two days being) the Sunday and the Monday, (this was) to teach (people) deliberateness (ta'liman li-l-anah). Had He willed to create it in an instant, He would have done so.

﴿And you set up rivals to Him﴾, partners and likenesses.

﴿That﴾, the One who created what has preceded,

﴿is the Lord of the worlds﴾, the Creator of all existent things, their Master, and their Nurturer.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 10:

﴿And He placed within it﴾, in the earth,

﴿firm mountains﴾, immovable mountains,

﴿from above it﴾. He chose to fix them above the earth so that the benefits of the mountains would be apparent to those who seek them, and so that it would be seen that the earth and the mountains are weights upon weights, all of them in need of one who holds them up, and He is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And He blessed﴾, with water, crops, trees and fruits,

﴿in it﴾, in the earth. It was said: He blessed it and increased its good.

﴿And He measured in it its sustenance﴾, the provisions of its people, their livelihoods, and whatever sets them right. Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, read: "and He apportioned in it its sustenance,"

﴿in four days﴾, in full four days. By "completion" he means the two days, as one says: "I travelled from Basra to Baghdad in ten [days], and to Kufa in fifteen," meaning, in the completion of fifteen. This estimation is necessary, for if it were taken literally it would be eight days, since He said: "He created the earth in two days," then He said: ﴿and He measured in it its sustenance in four days﴾, then He said: "Then He completed them as seven heavens in two days," which would contradict His saying "in six days" in another place. And in the hadith: "Allah (exalted be He) created the earth on Sunday and Monday, and created the mountains on Tuesday, and on Wednesday He created the trees, the water, the habitation and the ruin; those are four days. And on Thursday He created the heaven, and on Friday He created the stars, the sun, the moon and the angels, and He created Adam, upon him be peace, in the last hour of Friday." It was said: that is the hour in which the Resurrection will occur. "Sawa'in" [read by Ya'qub] is an attribute of the days, meaning: "in four days, equal, complete." "Sawa'un" [read by Yazid] in the nominative means: "they are equal." Others read it in the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning: "they were equal in equality," or as a circumstantial accusative.

﴿for those who ask﴾. This is connected to "measured," meaning: He measured its sustenance therein for the sake of those who seek it and need it, since everyone seeks food and asks for it. Or it is connected to an omitted element, as if it were said: "This restriction is for the sake of the one who asked: 'In how many days were the earth and what is in it created?!'"

﴿Then He turned to the heaven, and it was smoke. He said to it and to the earth: "Come both of you, willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly."﴾ This is a metaphor (majaz) for God's (Exalted is He) bringing the heaven into existence as He willed. The Arabs say: "So-and-so did such-and-such, then turned to doing such-and-such (thumma istawa ila 'amal kadha)," meaning that he completed the first and began the second. It is understood from this that the creation of the heaven came after the creation of the earth. This is also the view of Ibn 'Abbas (may God be pleased with them both). It is reported from him that he said: "The first thing God (Exalted is He) created was a jewel whose length and breadth were a thousand years' journey, within a journey of ten thousand years. He looked at it with awe, and it melted and trembled. Then smoke arose from it through the power of the fire upon it, and it rose up, and foam gathered. It stood above the water, so He made the foam into earth and the smoke into heaven." (p-229)

The meaning of commanding the heaven and the earth to come, and their obedience, is that He willed to bring them into being, and they did not resist Him; they came into existence as He willed them, and in this they were like an obedient subordinate when the command of a commanding master reaches him. The earth is mentioned together with the heaven in the command to come, although the earth was created two days before the heaven, because He first created the body of the earth without spreading it out (ghayr madhuwwa), then He spread it out after the creation of the heaven, as He said: ﴿And the earth after that He spread out﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 30]. So the meaning is: "Come in the form and attribute that you ought to come in: come, O earth, spread out, as a resting place and a cradle for your people; and come, O heaven, vaulted, as a roof over them."

The meaning of "ityan" (coming) is occurrence and taking place, as you say: "His work came pleasing (ataa 'amaluhu mardiyyan)." His saying "willingly or unwillingly" serves to show the effect of His power over them, and that their refusal to be affected by His power is impossible, just as you say to one under your authority: "You will do this, whether you want to or not," and you will do it willingly or unwillingly.

The accusative "ta'an" (تَأْتِيا, rendered here as the command itself) is in the position of a circumstantial state (hal), meaning "obeying, both of you," or "compelled, both of you." He did not say "ta'i'atayn" (طائِعَتَيْنِ, feminine dual) according to the wording, nor "ta'i'at" (طائِعاتٍ, feminine plural) according to the meaning, because they are heavens and earths (samawat and aradun), and since they were made addressable and responsive, and described with willingness and unwillingness, the masculine plural "ta'i'in" (طائِعِينَ) was used in place of "ta'i'at," as in His saying: ﴿ساجِدِينَ﴾ ("prostrating").

﴿So He completed them﴾, He perfected their creation. He said:

؎ وعَلَيْهِما مَسْرُودَتانِ قَضاهُما......................

The pronoun refers back to the heaven, because "the heaven" (al-sama') is a collective noun used for a genus (li-l-jins). It is also possible that the pronoun is an unspecified pronoun (damir mubham), explained by His words ﴿seven heavens﴾. The difference between the two accusatives is that the first is a circumstantial accusative (hal), and the second is a specifying accusative (tamyiz).

﴿in two days﴾, on the day of Thursday and Friday.

﴿And He revealed in each heaven its command﴾, what He commanded within it, and what He arranged of the creation of angels, fires, and other things.

﴿And We adorned the nearest heaven﴾, the one closest to the earth,

﴿with lamps﴾, with stars,

﴿and as a protection﴾, and We protected it from the eavesdroppers by means of the stars as a protection.

﴿That is the decree of the Almighty﴾, the Victorious who is not overcome,

﴿the All-Knowing﴾, of the places of affairs.

(p-230) ﴿Then if they turn away﴾ from faith, after this clarification,

﴿say, "I have warned you﴾, I have made you afraid,

﴿of a thunderbolt﴾, a punishment of severe impact, as if it were a thunderbolt. Its origin is a thunderclap accompanied by fire,

﴿like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 14:

﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them﴾. That is: they came to them from every side, and employed every stratagem with them, but they saw from them nothing but aversion. It is related from al-Hasan: "They warned them of the days of Allah concerning the nations before them, and of the punishment of the Hereafter." Here "an" (that) is in the sense of "ay" (namely), or it is the lightened form of the heavy "inna", its origin being "bi-annahu".

﴿Do not worship except Allah. They said﴾: that is, the people said:

﴿"If our Lord had willed"﴾, to send messengers, so the object of "willed" is omitted,

﴿"He would have sent down angels. So indeed we disbelieve in what you have been sent with"﴾. Its meaning is: "Then you are only humans, and you are not angels, so we do not believe in you, nor in what you have brought." Their saying "what you have been sent with" is not an acknowledgment of the sending; rather it is in the speech of the messengers, and it contains mockery, as Pharaoh said: ﴿Indeed your messenger who has been sent to you is surely a madman﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 27]. Their saying "So indeed we disbelieve in what you have been sent with" is an address from them to Hud, Salih, and the rest of the prophets who called them to belief in them. It is narrated that "the Quraysh sent 'Utba ibn Rabi'a, who was the best of them in speech, to speak with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and see what he wanted. He came to him while he was in al-Hatim, and he did not ask him anything except that he answered him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the surah up to His words: ﴿like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud﴾ [Fussilat 13]. He (Utba) adjured him by the ties of kinship, and held his hand over his mouth, and leapt up, fearing that the punishment would befall them. So he informed them of it, and said: 'I have known magic and poetry, and by Allah he is neither a magician nor a poet.' They said: 'You have indeed apostatized; did you not understand any word from him?' He said: 'No, and I did not find an answer to it.' Then 'Uthman ibn Maz'un said: 'By Allah, that is so that you may know that it is from the Lord of the worlds.'"

Then he explained what he had mentioned of the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud, and said:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 15:

﴿As for ʿAd, they were arrogant in the land without right﴾, i.e., they magnified themselves over its people (p-231) by means of what does not deserve magnification, namely strength and the greatness of their bodies. Or they seized control of the land without having any right to authority.

﴿And they said: "Who is stronger than us in strength?"﴾ They were people of tall bodies and great physique, and their strength reached the point that a man would uproot a rock from the mountain with his hand.

﴿Did they not see﴾, i.e., did they not know with a knowledge that takes the place of direct observation,

﴿that God, who created them, is stronger than them in strength﴾, more expansive than them in power, because He is capable of everything, while they are capable of some things by His empowering them.

﴿And they were denying Our signs﴾, coordinated with "they were arrogant". That is, they knew that they were true, but they denied them, as a depositary denies a deposit.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 16:**

﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind﴾, a violent wind that makes a roaring sound (tusarsiru), meaning that it makes a sound as it blows, from the *sarir* (screeching). Or [it means] a cold wind that burns with its intense cold. It is a repetition of the form of *al-sirr*, which is cold. It was said that it is the *dabur* (the west wind),

﴿in ominous days﴾, days that were unlucky for them. *Nahsat* (ominous) is read by Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Nafi'. *Nuhisa, nahsan* (he was made unlucky) is the opposite of *su'ida, sa'dan* (he was made fortunate), and *huwa nahis* (he is unlucky). As for *nahs*, it is either a lightened form of *nahs* (the same word), or an adjective on the pattern *fa'l*, or it is described by a verbal noun. They were from Wednesday at the end of Shawwal until the following Wednesday, and no people were punished except on a Wednesday.

﴿so that We might make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world﴾. He attributed the punishment (*'adhab*) to disgrace (*khizy*), which is humiliation, on the basis that it describes the punishment, as if he had said: "a punishment of disgrace", just as you say "the act of evil" (*fi'l al-su'*), meaning the evil act. This is supported by His saying: ﴿and the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing﴾. This is a metaphorical attribution (*al-isnad al-majazi*). Describing the punishment as disgraceful is more emphatic than describing them as disgraced. How far apart are your two statements: "he is a poet" and "he has poetry that is poetic".

﴿and they will not be helped﴾, from the idols they worshipped, in hope of their help for them.

﴿وَأمّا ثَمُودُ﴾ ("As for Thamud"), read with *raf'* (nominative) as the *mubtada'* (inceptive, the topic of the sentence). This is the most eloquent reading, because it comes after the particle of initiation and the predicate.

﴿فَهَدَيْناهُمْ﴾ ("then We guided them"). It is also read with *nasb* (accusative) as "الْمُفَضَّلُ" (al-mufaddal), by supposing a verb implied by "فَهَدَيْناهُمْ" that explains it. The meaning is: We made the right path clear to them.

﴿فاسْتَحَبُّوا العَمى عَلى الهُدى﴾ ("but they preferred blindness to guidance"): they chose disbelief over faith.

﴿فَأخَذَتْهم صاعِقَةُ العَذابِ﴾ ("so the thunderbolt of punishment seized them"): the calamity of the punishment.

﴿الهُونِ﴾ ("the humiliating"): meaning "al-hawan" (humiliation). The punishment is described by it as an intensification, or it is a *badal* (apposition) from it.

﴿بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ ("for what they used to earn"): for their earning, which is their polytheism and their sins.

Shaykh Abu Mansur said: "What has been mentioned of guidance may mean clarification, as we have explained, and it may mean creating the act of being guided in them, so that they became guided, and then they disbelieved after that and hamstrung the she-camel. This is because guidance attributed to creatures means clarification, and granting success, and creating the act of being guided. As for guidance attributed to creatures, it means only clarification."

The author of *al-Kashshaf* said concerning it: "If you say: Does the meaning of your saying 'I guided him' not amount to 'I placed guidance in him'? And the proof of this is your saying 'I guided him, so he was guided,' meaning the attainment of the goal and its occurrence, just as you say 'I deterred him, so he was deterred.' How then is it permissible to use it for mere indication? I say: The indication is that He empowered them, removed their excuses, and no excuse remained for them. So it is as if He achieved the goal in them by bringing about what necessitates it and calls for it."

He only resorted to this contrivance because he cannot interpret it as the creation of the act of being guided, since that contradicts his corrupt school of thought.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 18:

﴿And We delivered those who believed﴾, meaning: they chose guidance over blindness, from that thunderbolt,

﴿and they used to be wary﴾, of choosing blindness over guidance.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 19:

﴿And on the Day when the enemies of Allah are gathered to the Fire﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, from the first ones and the last ones, "nahshuru a'da'" (we gather the enemies), read by Nafi' and Ya'qub,

﴿then they will be driven back﴾, by holding back their first ones until their last ones [catch up], i.e., their vanguard is halted so that their rear ranks may join them. This is an expression for the great number of the people of the Fire. Its root is from "waza'tuhu" (I restrained him), i.e., "kaffatuhu" (I held him back).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 20:

﴿Until, when they reach it﴾: they arrive in its presence. The "mā" (ma) is superfluous (mazīdah), for emphasis (li-l-ta'kīd). The meaning of the emphasis is that the time of their coming to the Fire is certainly the time of testimony against them, and there is no way for it to be devoid of that.

﴿Their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against them concerning what they used to do.﴾ The testimony of the skins is by their touching the forbidden (ḥarām). It is also said: it is a metaphor (kināyah) for the private parts (furūj).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 21:

﴿And they will say to their skins: "Why did you testify against us?"﴾ Because it was grave to them that their skins were testifying against them. (p-233) ﴿They will say: "Allah has caused us to speak, He who causes everything to speak."﴾ That is, of the animals. The meaning is that our speech is not strange given the power of Allah, who is able to make every animal speak,

﴿And it is He who created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ He is capable of originating you the first time, and of restoring you and returning you to His recompense.

This is the commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 22:

﴿You used not to hide yourselves lest your hearing, your sight, or your skins should bear witness against you﴾. That is: you used to conceal yourselves behind walls and screens when committing indecent acts, and your concealment was not out of fear that your limbs (jawarih) would bear witness against you, because you did not know that they would testify against you. Rather, you were deniers of the Resurrection (al-ba'th) and of recompense (al-jaza') altogether.

﴿But you thought that Allah did not know much of what you were doing﴾. Rather, you concealed yourselves only because of your assumption that Allah does not know much of what you were doing, namely the hidden deeds of your actions.

Qur'an 41:23: ﴿And that opinion of yours which you held about your Lord has destroyed you; so you have become among the losers.﴾

Al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil): "And that opinion" (dhalikum) — that opinion is what destroyed you. "Dhalikum" is a mubtada' (subject), "zannukum" (your opinion) is the khabar (predicate), "alladhi zannantum bi-rabbikum" (which you held about your Lord) is its sifah (qualifying clause), and "aradakum" (has destroyed you) is a second khabar. Or, "zannukum" is a badal (apposition) for "dhalikum", and "aradakum" is the khabar.

﴿So you have become among the losers.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 24:

﴿Whether they endure patiently, the Fire is their abode.﴾ That is: if they endure patiently, patience will not benefit them, and they will not be released through it from dwelling in the Fire.

﴿And if they ask to be shown favour, they will not be among those shown favour.﴾ That is: if they seek contentment (al-ridā), they will not be among those who are content with them. Or: if they ask for al-'utba (ʿutba) — which means returning to them what they love, out of distress at what they are in — they will not be granted al-'utba; they will not be given it, and it will not be answered for them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 25:

﴿And We appointed for them﴾ means: We decreed for the polytheists of Makkah. It is said: "These are two garments qayd-an (qayḍān)," meaning: two similar ones. And al-muqāyaḍah (exchange) is al-mu'āwaḍah (mutual exchange). It is also said: We empowered over them,

﴿companions﴾: intimate friends from among the devils. It is the plural of qarīn (companion), like His saying: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 36].

﴿And they made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them﴾: that is, their deeds that had already passed, and what they were resolved upon; or, what was before them of the affairs of this world and the pursuit of desires, and what was behind them of the matter of the final outcome, and that there is no resurrection and no reckoning.

﴿And the word has come true against them﴾: the word of punishment,

﴿among nations﴾: among a group of nations. Its place in i'rab is an accusative of circumstance (ḥāl) from the pronoun in ʿalayhim, meaning: the word has come true against them while being among a group of nations,

﴿that passed away before them﴾: before the people of Makkah,

﴿of jinn and humankind. Indeed they were losers﴾: this is an explanation (ta'līl) for their deserving the punishment. The pronoun (in "they were") refers to them and to the nations.

ۚ"And those who disbelieve say: Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during its recitation, so that you may prevail."

Al-Nasafi's commentary: "Those who disbelieve say: 'Do not listen to this Qur'an' when it is recited, 'and make noise during it, so that you may prevail'; and oppose it with speech that is not understandable, so that you disturb it and overcome its recitation. Al-laghw (idle talk, nonsense) is that which falls from speech and has no benefit in it."

"So We will surely make those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment." It is permissible that by "those who disbelieve" is meant these people who engage in idle talk, and those who instruct others to engage in idle talk specifically, and that He mentions "those who disbelieve" in general so that they may be included under this mention.

"And We will surely recompense them with the worst of what they used to do," i.e., the greatest punishment, for their worst deeds, and that is disbelief.

That is the jazā' of the enemies of Allah: that (ḏālika) is a demonstrative referring to the worst (al-asw'a). It must be that the estimated (taqdīr) phrase is "the worst recompense of what they used to do," so that this demonstrative may be correct.

"The Fire" (al-nār) is either an apposition (ʿaṭf bayān) to "the recompense," or the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada').

"For them therein is the abode of eternity" means: the Fire itself is the abode of eternity, just as you say, "For you in this house is the house of joy," while you mean the house itself.

"Recompense" (jazā'): that is, they were recompensed with that as a recompense.

"Because they used to deny Our signs."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 29:

﴿And those who disbelieve say: Our Lord, show us﴾. It is read with a sukun on the ra' (أَرْنا), because of the heaviness of the kasra, just as they said of فَخِذٌ (fakhidh) and فَخْذٌ (fakhdh). Makki, Shami and Abu Bakr read it this way. Abu 'Amr read it with ikhtilas (a rapid, truncated pronunciation of the vowel).

[p. 235] ﴿the two who led us astray﴾, that is, the two devils who led us astray,

﴿of the jinn and of mankind﴾, because the devil is of two kinds: a jinn devil and a human devil. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And thus We appointed for every prophet an enemy, devils of mankind and jinn﴾ [al-An'am: 112]. ﴿We will place them beneath our feet so that they will be among the lowest﴾, in the Fire, as recompense for their having misled us.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 30:

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah,"﴾ meaning: they uttered the tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness),

﴿and then remained steadfast﴾, then they held firm to the affirmation and what it requires. It is related from al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Be steadfast in deed just as you were steadfast in word." It is also related from him that he recited it and then said: "What do you say about it?" They said: "They did not commit sin." He said: "You have taken the matter to its extreme." They said: "Then what do you say?" He said: "They did not return to worshipping idols." It is related from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: "They did not slink away like foxes," meaning: they were not hypocrites. It is related from Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him: "They made their deeds sincere." It is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "They performed the obligations." It is related from al-Fudayl: "They were detached from the transient and desired the everlasting." It has also been said: the reality of steadfastness is "remaining firm after affirmation, not fleeing after affirmation."

﴿The angels will descend upon them﴾, at the time of death,

﴿saying: "Do not fear and do not grieve"﴾. "An" here is in the sense of "ay" (that is), or it is the light form of the heavy "anna," and its original form is "bi-annahu la takhafu," with the "ha" being the pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n), meaning: "Do not fear what you are about to face,"

﴿and do not grieve﴾ over what you have left behind. Fear is distress that afflicts a person due to anticipating something disliked, while grief is distress that afflicts a person due to the occurrence of the loss of something beneficial or the arrival of something harmful. The meaning is that Allah has decreed for you security from every distress, so you will never taste it.

﴿And rejoice in the Garden which you were promised﴾, in this world. Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tirmidhi said: "The angels of the Most Merciful will descend upon them at the moment the souls separate from the bodies: 'Do not fear the loss of faith, and do not grieve over what was of disobedience, and rejoice in entering the gardens which you were promised in bygone times.'"

﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾. Just as the devils are companions (qurana') and brothers of the disobedient, so too the angels are allies of the God-fearing (al-muttaqin) and their beloved in both abodes.

﴿And therein you shall have whatever your souls desire﴾, of bliss.

﴿And therein you shall have whatever you ask for﴾, meaning, whatever you wish for.

﴿نُـزُلا﴾ (a welcome provision) is the provision of the *nazīl* (the guest), who is the *ḍayf* (the guest). Its placement in the accusative is as a *ḥāl* (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the subject) from the omitted pronoun *hāʾ*, or from *mā*.

﴿مِن غَفُورٍ رَحِيمٍ﴾ (from One Most Forgiving, Most Merciful) is a *naʿt* (qualifying adjective) of it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 33:

﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah﴾: he is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who called to tawhid (affirmation of the oneness of Allah).

﴿and does righteous deeds﴾: sincerely.

﴿and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"﴾: boasting of Islam, or believing in it, or [it refers to] his companions (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him), or the muezzins (mu'adhdhinun), or all the guides (hudah) and callers (du'at) to Allah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 34:

﴿And good and evil are not equal. Repel [evil] with that which is better.﴾ He means that good and evil differ in themselves, so take hold of the good that is better than its counterpart when two goods confront you, and repel with it the evil that comes to you from some of your enemies. For example, if a man wrongs you with some injury, the good is to pardon him, and that which is better is to do good to him in return for his wrong to you, such as when he reviles you and you praise him, or when he kills your child and you ransom his child from the hand of his enemy.

﴿Then, verily, he between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a close friend.﴾ For when you do that, your hostile opponent turns into like a close, warm friend, being sincerely devoted to you. Then he said:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 35:

﴿And none is granted it⦆ means: and none is granted this quality, which is repaying evil with good,

﴿except those who are patient﴾, except the people of patience,

﴿and none is granted it except one of great good fortune﴾, except a man of goodness, who is granted a great portion of good. The reason He did not say, "Repel with that which is better," is that it is in the sense of a speaker who said, "How shall I act?", so it was said, "Repel with that which is better." It was also said that "lā" (لا) is added for emphasis, and the meaning is, "The good deed and the evil deed are not equal." Following this interpretation, the analogy would have been to say, "Repel with that which is good (حَسَنَة)," but He placed "that which is better (الَّتِي هي أحْسَنُ)" in the place of "the good (الْحَسَنَة)," so as to be more eloquent in repelling with good, because whoever repels with the finer thing finds it easy to repel with what is lesser than it.

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding "with that which is better": patience at the time of anger, forbearance at the time of ignorance, and pardon at the time of injury. He interpreted "ḥaẓẓ" (great portion) as reward. It is related from al-Hasan: "By Allah, no portion is greater than Paradise." It was also said: it was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, who was a hostile enemy harming the Prophet (ﷺ), and then became a sincere friend.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 36:

﴿And if an incitement from Satan should incite you, then seek refuge in Allah﴾. The nazgh (incitement) is like a prodding (nakhs), and Satan incites (yanzighu) the human being as if he were prodding him, urging him toward what is not fitting. He made the incitement (nazgh) into one who incites (nazigh), as it is said: "Its grandeur has become great" (jadda jiddu-hu). Or the meaning is: "And if one who incites should incite you," describing Satan with the verbal noun, or referring to his enticement (taswil). The meaning is: "And if Satan turns you away from what you were enjoined to do, namely repelling [evil] with what is better."

﴿So seek refuge in Allah﴾ from his evil, and persist in your forbearance, and do not obey him.

﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing﴾ of your seeking refuge,

﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of Satan's incitement.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 37:

﴿And among His signs﴾, which indicate His oneness,

﴿the night and the day﴾, in their succeeding one another according to a known measure, and their alternating according to an apportioned quantity,

﴿and the sun and the moon﴾, in their being specified with a determined course and a fixed light,

﴿Do not prostrate yourselves to the sun or to the moon﴾, for they are created, even if their benefits are many,

﴿but prostrate yourselves to Allah, who created them, if it is Him you worship﴾. The pronoun in "khalaqahunna" (who created them) refers either to the signs, or to the night, the day, the sun and the moon, because the rule for a plural of non-rational things is the rule of the feminine singular, or of the feminine plurals. You say: "al-aqlam baraytuha" (I sharpened the pens), and "baraytuhunna" (I sharpened them).

Perhaps some of them were prostrating to the sun and the moon, like the Sabians in their worship of the stars, and they claimed that by prostrating to them they intended prostration to Allah (exalted is He). So they were forbidden this intermediary, and they were commanded to direct their prostration to the Face of Allah sincerely, "if it is Him you worship," and they were monotheists, not polytheists, for whoever worships another alongside Allah is not a worshipper of Allah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 38:

﴿So if they are arrogant, then those who are with your Lord﴾ — i.e., the angels,

﴿glorify Him by night and day, and they never tire﴾ — they do not grow weary. The meaning is: if they are arrogant, and do not comply with what they were commanded, and refuse except the intermediary, then leave them to themselves, for Allah (Exalted) never lacks a worshipper and a prostrator in sincerity. He has the devoted worshippers who are brought near, who declare Him free of rivals by night and day. And "with your Lord" is an expression for nearness, rank, and honour. The place of prostration according to us is at "they never tire," and according to al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) it is at "you worship" (ta'budun). The first is more cautious (ahwat).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 41, verse 40:

﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs﴾, they incline away from the truth regarding Our proofs, by defaming them. It is said: "*alhada al-hafir*" (ألْحَدَ الحافِرُ) and "*lahada*" (لَحَدَ), when he (the digger) deviated from uprightness, so he dug in a side (niche). The term was then borrowed for deviation in the interpretation of the signs of the Qur'an away from the direction of soundness and uprightness. "*Yalhadūn*" (يَلْحَدُونَ) is the reading of Hamza.

﴿They are not hidden from Us﴾, a warning to them for distorting (the signs).

﴿So is he who is thrown into the Fire better, or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ This is an illustration of the disbeliever and the believer.

﴿Do whatever you wish﴾, this is an extreme form of threat and an exaggeration in warning.

﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾, so He will recompense you for it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 41:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder⁠—⁠﴾, that is, the Qur'an. Because of their disbelief in it, they slandered it and distorted its interpretation.

﴿when it comes to them﴾, when it comes to them. The predicate of "inna" (indeed) is omitted, meaning: "they will be punished," or "they will perish," or "those are called from a far place," and what lies between them is a parenthetical interjection (i'tiraḍ).

﴿And indeed it is a Mighty Book﴾, that is, invincible (manī'), protected by the protection of Allah.

(p-239) ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it﴾ — alteration (tabdil) or contradiction (tanaqud),

﴿from before it or from behind it﴾ — i.e., in any respect whatsoever,

﴿a revelation from One who is All-Wise, Praiseworthy﴾ — deserving of praise.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 43:

﴿Nothing is said to you﴾, meaning: nothing is said to you by the disbelievers of your people,

﴿except what was said to the messengers before you﴾, meaning: none other than what the disbelieving peoples of the messengers said to them of hurtful words and slanders against the revealed books,

﴿Indeed your Lord is Possessor of forgiveness﴾, and mercy toward His prophets,

﴿and Possessor of painful punishment﴾, toward their enemies. It is also permissible that it means: "Your Lord says to you nothing but the like of what He said to the messengers before you," and the thing said is His saying: "Indeed your Lord is Possessor of forgiveness and Possessor of painful punishment."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 44:

﴿And if We had made it﴾ (i.e., the Reminder),

﴿a non-Arabic Qur'an﴾ (i.e., in the language of the non-Arabs). They, out of their obstinacy, would say: "Why was the Qur'an not revealed in the language of the non-Arabs?" So it was said in reply to them: if it were as they propose,

﴿they would surely have said: "Why have its verses not been made clear?"﴾ (i.e., explained in the language of the Arabs, so that we may understand it), out of obstinacy,

﴿"What, a non-Arabic (scripture) and an Arab (messenger)?"﴾ With two hamzas, according to Kufan (reader) other than Hafs. The hamza is for denial, meaning: they would have denied it and said: "A non-Arabic Qur'an and an Arab messenger," or "an Arab addressed by it." The rest (of the readers) read it with a single extended hamza, as an interrogative. Al-a'jami (the non-Arabic) is one who is not eloquent and whose speech is not understood, whether he is of the non-Arabs or of the Arabs. Al-'ajami is one related to the nation of the non-Arabs, whether eloquent or not. The meaning is that whatever way the signs of Allah came to them, they found in them an occasion for obstinacy, because they do not seek the truth, and only follow their desires. This also implies that if He had revealed it in the language of the non-Arabs, it would have been a Qur'an, and so it is evidence for Abu Hanifa (may Allah be pleased with him) regarding the permissibility of prayer when one recites in Persian.

﴿Say: it is﴾ (i.e., the Qur'an),

﴿for those who believe, guidance﴾, a directing to the truth,

﴿and healing﴾, for what is in the breasts of doubt, since doubt is a sickness,

﴿but as for those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness﴾. It is in the genitive position, being coordinated (ma'tuf) on "those who believe," meaning: it is for those who believe a guidance and healing, and it is for those who do not believe a deafness in their ears, i.e., hardness of hearing. However, this involves coordination over two governing elements, which is permissible according to al-Akhfash; or (it is in the nominative), and its estimate is: "and those who do not believe, it is in their ears a deafness," with the subject elided; or "in their ears there is deafness from it."

﴿And it is﴾ (i.e., the Qur'an),

﴿for them blindness﴾, darkness and doubt.

﴿They are called from a far place﴾. The meaning is that, because of their non-acceptance and failure to benefit, it is as if they are being called to faith in the Qur'an from a place from which they cannot hear, because of the great distance. It was also said: they will be called on the Day of Resurrection from a far place by the worst of names.

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, but it was disputed about.﴾ Some of them said: it is true, and some of them said: it is false, just as your people disputed about your Book.

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, [regarding] the delay of the punishment,

﴿it would have been decided between them﴾, He would have destroyed them with total annihilation (istiʾṣāl). It was also said: the preceding word is the promise of the Resurrection, and that disputes will be settled on that Day. Had it not been for that, it would have been decided between them in this world. ﴿And indeed they﴾, and indeed the disbelievers,

﴿are in disquieting doubt about it﴾, a doubt that causes unease.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 47:

﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour﴾, i.e., the knowledge of its establishment is referred to Him; that is, the one who is asked must say: "Allah knows that."

﴿And no fruit comes out of its sheaths﴾ — read by Medina, Syria and Hafs without an alif (ثَمَرَاتٍ becomes thamarat, with the alif), while the others read it without an alif (thamarin/thamarat without alif, as the reading of the remaining Qurra' has it) —

﴿from its sheaths﴾, i.e., its coverings, before they split open; the plural of "kumm" (kamm, a sheath or covering).

﴿Nor does any female conceive﴾, i.e., her pregnancy,

﴿nor give birth except with His knowledge﴾. That is, nothing occurs of the emergence of a fruit, nor of the conception of a pregnant woman, nor of the delivery of one who gives birth, except that He is aware of it. He knows the number of days of the pregnancy and its hours, and its conditions, whether the child is born prematurely or full-term, male or female, beautiful or ugly, and other than that.

﴿And on the Day He calls to them: "Where are My partners?"﴾ He attributed them to Himself according to their own claim, and its explanation is in His saying: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?" and in it is mockery and rebuke.

﴿They will say: "We have informed You"﴾, i.e., we have made You aware. It was also said: "We have told You," and this is the more apparent, since Allah (exalted is He) was already knowing of that, and informing one who knows is impossible; but informing one who knows of a thing is realized by what he already knows about it, unless the meaning is: "You now know from our hearts that we do not bear that false testimony, for when He knows it from their souls, it is as if they had informed Him."

﴿None of us is a witness﴾, i.e., none of us today testifies that You have a partner; none of us but is one who affirms Your oneness. Or: none of us sees them, because they have gone astray from them, and their gods have gone astray from them, so they do not see them at the time of reproach. It was also said: this is the speech of the partners, i.e., none of us is a witness testifying to what they attributed to us of partnership.

﴿And what they used to invoke will have strayed from them﴾, meaning what they used to worship,

﴿before﴾, meaning in the world,

﴿and they will think﴾, meaning and they will be certain,

﴿that there is for them no escape﴾, meaning no place of flight.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 49:

﴿Man does not tire﴾ of asking, i.e., does not grow weary (yamall),

﴿man﴾, i.e., the disbeliever, as indicated by His words: ﴿And I do not think the Hour will be established﴾ [Fussilat: 50]. ﴿of asking for good﴾, i.e., of seeking abundance in wealth and blessing. The original construction is "min du'a'ihi al-khayra" (his asking for good), but the agent has been deleted and the verbal noun has been made to refer to its object (idafah to the maf'ul).

﴿But when evil touches him﴾, i.e., poverty,

﴿he becomes despairing﴾, i.e., of good,

﴿and hopeless﴾, i.e., of mercy. Intensification is achieved in two ways: through the pattern "fa'ul" and through repetition. "Al-qunut" is that the trace of despair appears upon a person so that he shrinks and is broken, i.e., he cuts off hope of God's bounty and mercy. This is the attribute of the disbeliever, as indicated by His (exalted) words: ﴿Indeed, no one despairs of the mercy of God except the disbelieving people﴾ [Yusuf: 87].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 50:

﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after some adversity had touched him, he would surely say: "This is mine (by right)."﴾ And when We relieve him of [hardship], granting him health after sickness, or ease after straitened circumstances, he says: "This is mine," i.e., "This is my due; it has come to me because I have deserved it by the good, the favour, and the righteous deeds that I possess." Or [it means]: "This is mine; it will not depart from me."

﴿And I do not think the Hour will be established﴾, i.e., I do not think it will come to be established.

﴿And if I am returned to my Lord﴾, as the Muslims say,

﴿indeed I shall have with Him﴾, with Allah,

﴿the best [reward]﴾, i.e., Paradise, or the best state of honour and blessing, weighing the affair of the Hereafter against the affair of this world.

﴿Then We will surely inform those who disbelieved of what they did﴾, i.e., We will surely inform them of the reality of the deeds they performed which necessitate punishment,

﴿and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾, a harsh punishment that does not slacken for them.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 51:**

﴿When We bestow favour upon man, he turns away﴾. This is another form of man's transgression. When God afflicts him with a blessing, the blessing makes him arrogant, so he forgets the Benefactor and turns away from giving Him thanks.

﴿And turns aside with his side﴾: he distances himself from the remembrance and supplication of God, or he becomes conceited, proud and self-aggrandising. Its real meaning is that his side is placed in the position of his self (nafs), because the place of a thing is its direction, and it is put in the rank of its self. From this is the saying of the scribes: "I wrote to his direction and to his honoured side," meaning himself and his essence. It is as if He said: "he turned aside with his self."

﴿And when evil touches him﴾: harm and poverty.

﴿Then he is one of lengthy supplication﴾: abundant. That is, he persists in constant supplication, takes to earnest entreaty and humble pleading. The term "breadth" (ʿarīd) is used metaphorically for the abundance and continuity of supplication, and it is a property of physical bodies, just as "thickness" (ghilaẓ) is used metaphorically for the severity of punishment. There is no contradiction between His saying "despairing and despondent" (fa-yaʾūs qanūṭ) and His saying ﴿then he is one of lengthy supplication﴾, because the first describes one group and the second describes another group. Or: he is despondent on land and of lengthy supplication at sea; or he is despondent in the heart and of lengthy supplication with the tongue; or he is despondent of the idol and of lengthy supplication to God (exalted is He).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 52:

﴿Say: Tell me,﴾ inform me,

﴿if it is﴾ the Qur'an,

﴿from Allah, and you disbelieve in it,﴾ then you deny that it is from Allah,

﴿who is further astray﴾ than you? Except that he placed his words: ﴿than one who is in extreme opposition﴾ in the place of "than you," to explain their condition and their attribute.

(p-243) ﴿We will show them Our signs on the horizons﴾ — that is, the conquest of lands, to the east and to the west —

﴿and within themselves﴾ — the conquest of Makkah.

﴿until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ — that is, the Qur'an, or Islam.

﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is over all things a witness?﴾ The place of "bi-Rabbika" (concerning your Lord) is in the nominative case, as it is the agent (fa'il), and the object is omitted. His saying ﴿that He is over all things a witness﴾ is a substitute (badal) for it. Its estimated form is: "Is it not sufficient for them that your Lord is over all things a witness?" That is: "Is it not sufficient for them the testimony of your Lord over all things?" Its meaning is that this promised manifestation of the signs of Allah on the horizons and within themselves — they will see it and witness it, and at that point they will become clear that the Qur'an is a revelation from the Knower of the Unseen, who is over all things a witness.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 54:

﴿Behold, they are in doubt﴾, i.e., in suspicion (shakk),

﴿about the meeting with their Lord. Behold, He surely encompasses all things﴾, He is knowing of the totalities of things and their details, their outward and their inward aspects, so that nothing hidden is concealed from Him, and He will therefore recompense them for their disbelief and their doubt concerning the meeting with their Lord.
